article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Indica-dominant hybrid
Genetics: Jungle Cake × Strawberry Shortcake
Breeder: Jungle Boys
THC Content: 20%–28%
CBD Content: Generally below 1%
Terpene Profile: Myrcene , Beta-Caryophyllene , Linalool
Primary Flavors: Strawberry cream, vanilla cake
Flowering Time (Indoor): Approximately 8–10 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: Late September to mid-October
Indoor Yield: Moderate to high
Outdoor Yield: High
Grow Difficulty: Moderate

Frosted Cake makes its strongest first impression before it is ever smoked. The buds can develop an almost powdered appearance as pale trichomes spread across tightly formed green and purple flower, creating the frosted surface suggested by the name. Its aroma, however, is considerably less simple than sugary cake. Strawberry cream and vanilla sweetness sit over damp earth, pepper, diesel, and a peculiar savory funk that can occasionally resemble mild cheese.

Jungle Boys created the cultivar by crossing Jungle Cake with Strawberry Shortcake, combining a potent modern Cake hybrid with a berry-forward strain carrying an entirely different aromatic direction. The resulting marijuana strain delivers plenty of dessert character without abandoning the pungent gas and earth underneath. Effects follow a similarly layered path, often opening with pleasant cerebral euphoria before settling into a heavier, slower physical state that makes the cultivar better suited to relaxed afternoons and evenings than highly structured daytime activity.
Genetics and Lineage

The direct genetic formula is Jungle Cake × Strawberry Shortcake. Jungle Cake contributes a substantial portion of the cultivar’s potency, resin production, dense structure, and creamy-gas character. That parent descends from Wedding Cake and White Fire #43, placing sweet pastry, earthy Kush, lemon fuel, and OG-style pungency into the family tree. Wedding Cake adds dense flower and dessert sweetness, while White Fire #43 brings a sharper fuel-driven edge.

Strawberry Shortcake takes the pedigree in a fruitier direction. Rather than simply adding another Cake-family parent, it introduces the sweet berry character responsible for much of the finished hybrid’s strawberry identity. Depending on the selection, that influence can resemble fresh strawberries, berry preserves, strawberry cream, or even slightly tart fruit. Against Jungle Cake’s gas and dough, the contrast creates a profile that feels richer than a conventional sweet strain.

The combination also explains the plant’s dramatic appearance. Both sides can contribute strong resin production, while Jungle Cake supplies substantial flower density and the Strawberry Shortcake influence can bring colorful accents and sweeter aromatics. Frosted Cake subsequently proved useful enough in breeding that Jungle Boys crossed it back into Jungle Cake to create Frosted Jungle, reinforcing how valuable the cultivar became beyond finished flower alone.
Effects and Experience

The beginning usually carries more mental lift than its indica-heavy reputation might suggest. Mood can improve quickly, conversation becomes easier, and familiar entertainment may feel more engaging. The cerebral portion tends to be euphoric rather than sharply stimulating, creating a slightly floaty state that works well with music, movies, gaming, or unstructured social time. Creativity may increase, although attention can become less disciplined as the high expands.

Physical relaxation gradually catches up. Muscles loosen, movement becomes slower, and the initial mental brightness begins to soften around the edges. Instead of an abrupt sedative drop, the transition often feels progressive. Moderate servings may leave experienced cannabis consumers pleasantly relaxed without making them completely inactive, particularly during the first half of the session.

Larger amounts reveal why Frosted Cake is usually placed on the heavier side of the hybrid spectrum. Body weight becomes more pronounced, motivation can fade, and the earlier euphoria develops into a hazier, more inward-focused state. Strong batches may reach the upper 20% THC range or beyond, so consumers with limited tolerance should give each dose adequate time before consuming more. Overconsumption can lead to dry mouth, red eyes, dizziness, impaired short-term memory, or anxiety.
Medical Benefits

For medical marijuana consumers, the cultivar’s combination of mood elevation and later physical relaxation may be attractive when emotional stress and bodily discomfort occur together. The initial mental shift can temporarily make repetitive thoughts or everyday pressure feel less intrusive, while the heavier second phase may reduce awareness of muscle tension, soreness, or generalized discomfort.

Evening use is particularly compatible with the way the effects develop. Rather than feeling immediately sleepy, a consumer may first experience a period of comfortable euphoria before the body begins slowing down. Appetite can increase during this later stage, and larger servings may make rest or sleep easier for people who already respond to THC with sedation.

Frosted Cake has not been clinically proven to treat anxiety, insomnia, depression, chronic pain , appetite disorders, or another medical condition. Individual response to cannabis depends on dosage, THC concentration, medications, physiology, tolerance, and the chemistry of the specific batch. High-THC weed may also increase anxiety in susceptible consumers, so therapeutic use should remain conservative and individualized.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Strawberry sweetness provides the most recognizable top note, but it quickly develops into something creamier and more complex. Fresh flower may smell like berries folded into vanilla frosting or strawberry cake batter. As the buds are broken apart, heavier notes appear underneath: damp earth, black pepper, dough, fuel, and occasionally a mild savory or cheese-like funk.

Myrcene commonly supports the earthy, musky side of the profile, while beta-caryophyllene contributes pepper and spice. Linalool can reinforce the softer floral and creamy impressions, and limonene may add a brighter citrus edge to certain batches. Because phenotype, cultivation, harvest timing, and curing all influence terpene concentration, not every example will emphasize the same combination.

The inhale generally begins sweet, with strawberry, vanilla, and creamy pastry flavors appearing before the heavier genetics take over. Earth and pepper develop through the middle, while diesel and savory funk become clearer during the exhale. Well-cured flower leaves behind a lingering mixture of berry cream and gas rather than disappearing into generic sweetness. That contrast is central to the cultivar’s appeal: dessert flavors lead the experience, but the finish still tastes unmistakably like potent cannabis.
Growing Information

Frosted Cake generally grows as a medium-sized hybrid with enough structural strength to support dense flowering sites. Its Jungle Cake ancestry can produce vigorous branching and moderate stretch after the switch to flowering, so indoor growers benefit from shaping the canopy during vegetation. Topping creates several productive leaders, while low-stress training can spread those branches across the available light footprint.

An indoor flowering period of roughly eight to ten weeks is appropriate for the established genetic line. Flower density increases considerably late in bloom, and trichomes can cover both the calyxes and nearby sugar leaves with a conspicuous pale layer. Because those compact buds can trap moisture, strong airflow and controlled humidity become especially important during the final weeks. Selective removal of congested interior leaves and weak lower shoots can help without unnecessarily stripping productive foliage.

Outdoor plants appreciate strong sunlight, generous root space, and a relatively dry finish to the season. Harvest commonly falls between late September and mid-October depending on phenotype, climate, and latitude. Production can be substantial where the plant receives adequate light and nutrition, although flower quality and resin coverage are greater attractions than raw yield alone. Growers should judge maturity through trichome development, calyx swelling, pistil progression, and overall plant condition rather than harvesting simply because the buds already appear heavily frosted.
FAQ
What are the genetics of Frosted Cake?

The Jungle Boys version is Jungle Cake × Strawberry Shortcake. Jungle Cake contributes Wedding Cake and White Fire #43 influence, while Strawberry Shortcake supplies much of the sweet berry character.
Who bred Frosted Cake?

Jungle Boys created the Frosted Cake cultivar covered here. It is also commonly called Frosted Cakes. Other unrelated strains have appeared under similar names, so breeder identification matters when researching genetics.
Is Frosted Cake indica or sativa?
It is generally considered an indica-dominant hybrid. The experience often begins with noticeable cerebral euphoria, but physical relaxation becomes increasingly important as the high progresses.
What does Frosted Cake taste like?

Typical flavors include strawberry, sweet cream, vanilla cake, berries, earth, pepper, diesel, and mild savory funk. Some batches lean heavily toward strawberry dessert, while others show more Jungle Cake gas.
How long does Frosted Cake take to flower?
Indoor flowering generally requires approximately eight to ten weeks. Outdoor plants usually reach maturity from late September into mid-October under suitable Northern Hemisphere conditions.
Final Thoughts on Frosted Cake

Frosted Cake demonstrates how dessert genetics can remain sweet without becoming predictable. Jungle Cake provides dense resin, pastry-like richness, Kush depth, and sharp fuel, while Strawberry Shortcake introduces berry sweetness that changes the entire aromatic direction of the cross. The result can smell like strawberry frosting when first opened yet finish with earth, pepper, diesel, and savory cannabis funk after the flower is smoked.

There is plenty of substance behind the flavor. The high moves from comfortable cerebral euphoria toward deeper body relaxation, the plants finish within a practical commercial flowering window, and mature buds can develop exceptional trichome coverage. For consumers who enjoy Cake-family weed but want something fruitier than the familiar vanilla-and-gas formula, Frosted Cake offers a distinctive variation. Its reputation ultimately rests on that contrast: sweet enough to earn the dessert name, pungent enough to satisfy traditional cannabis tastes, and frosty enough that the name makes sense before the jar is even opened.
